statement: Requirements are set for protecting data while it is processed. Secrets and sensitive values are kept out of logs and code, held in a controlled secrets store and exposed only when needed. Shared or multi-tenant platforms isolate each user's or tenant's data from others, and this is checked through testing. Proof is the standard, secrets store settings and isolation test results.
why_asked: Data is most exposed while in use, and leaked secrets or cross-tenant access defeat encryption of stored data.
how_to_ask: Ask whether the data protection standard covers data in use, then ask how secrets are kept out of code and logs. Ask for tenant isolation tests. Example probe: "Where do application secrets live, and how do you know none appear in logs or source code?"
question: Does your organization protect data while it is processed by controlling secrets handling and isolating one tenant's data from another's?
expected_evidence: Data protection standard section on data in use; secrets manager configuration and code or log scan results; tenant isolation test reports or container isolation settings; covering the audit period
good_looks_like: The standard has explicit requirements for data in use. Secrets are held in a secrets manager and kept out of code and logs. Multi-tenant platforms show tested isolation of each tenant's data.
test: Obtain the standard, secrets settings and isolation test results. Check the standard states data in use requirements. Sample three applications and check secrets are in the store and absent from sampled code and logs. Check the latest isolation test passed. Pass if all hold.
baseline_risk: Secrets leak through code and logs, and one customer's data becomes visible to another.
applicability: Applies to the secrets elements everywhere; the tenant isolation element applies if the organization runs shared or multi-tenant platforms.
